ordered_diagnoses: Breast Cancer with Axillary Lymph Node Metastasis

facts.raw_span: A 48-year-old woman
type 2 diabetes
hypertension
bilateral breast lumps of one-week duration
no family history of breast or ovarian cancer
a 4 × 4 cm hard lump in the lower inner quadrant fixed to the chest wall
MRI showed a 3.8 × 3.5 cm irregular spiculated mass in the left breast suspicious for malignancy
a 2.3 × 1.5 cm well-defined lesion in the right breast with a type 1 contrast enhancement pattern (< 6% probability of malignancy)
bilateral axillary lymphadenopathy
poorly cohesive clusters of ductal cells with pleomorphism, hyperchromasia, and prominent nucleoli
infiltrative duct cell carcinoma that was estrogen- and progesterone-receptor positive
FNAC of the left axillary lymph node showed similar malignant cells

support_spans: MRI showed a 3.8 × 3.5 cm irregular spiculated mass in the left breast suspicious for malignancy
poorly cohesive clusters of ductal cells with pleomorphism, hyperchromasia, and prominent nucleoli

concepts.why: The patient's left breast lump was diagnosed as infiltrative ductal carcinoma based on MRI, FNAC, and core-needle biopsy results.

support_spans: a 2.3 × 1.5 cm well-defined lesion in the right breast with a type 1 contrast enhancement pattern (< 6% probability of malignancy)
concepts.why: The patient's right breast lump was suspected to be a fibroadenoma based on its well-defined appearance and low probability of malignancy on MRI.

support_spans: bilateral breast lumps of one-week duration
contradict_spans: poorly cohesive clusters of ductal cells with pleomorphism, hyperchromasia, and prominent nucleoli
concepts.why: The patient's bilateral breast lumps could be indicative of ductal carcinoma in situ, but the presence of malignant cells on FNAC suggests invasive disease.
